name: Microprobing
description: Direct electrical contact with exposed IC conductors using precision probes to observe or inject signals at the circuit level. Covers probe station operation, tungsten and platinum probe needle manipulation, signal observation on internal buses, data extraction from memory arrays, and active probing to inject signals or force logic states. Requires decapsulated or partially decapsulated samples.

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands microprobing concepts, equipment, and applications
evidence: Can explain the purpose and capabilities of a probe station for IC analysis
Understands the difference between passive (observation) and active (injection) probing
Aware of probe types (passive tungsten/platinum needles, active high-impedance probes) and their applications

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Operates probe station and makes contact with exposed conductors under supervision
evidence: Navigates a decapped IC on the probe station using optical microscopy
Successfully lands probe needles on bond pads and top-metal conductors
Observes digital signals (clock, data bus) on exposed IC conductors with guidance
Follows anti-static and ESD safety procedures during probing sessions

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently probes IC signals and extracts data from internal buses and memory
evidence: Identifies target signal lines on decapped ICs using layout analysis or optical inspection
Extracts data from internal buses (address, data, control) via passive probing
Reads memory contents by probing memory array bit lines and word lines
Completed microprobing assessments on 3+ different IC targets independently

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Performs active probing on sub-micron features; develops probing strategies; mentors team
evidence: Probes sub-micron features on advanced process nodes using FIB-exposed landing pads
Performs active probing to inject signals, force logic states, or bypass security fuses
Develops probing strategies based on IC layout analysis and known circuit function
Mentors team on probe station operation, needle manipulation, and signal integrity

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Recognized authority on microprobing; defines methodology; specifies probe station equipment
evidence: Defines the lab's microprobing methodology and capability requirements
Evaluates and specifies probe station equipment (manual, semi-auto, AFM-based)
Develops novel probing techniques for advanced packaging and process technologies
Provides expert consultation on probing resistance and anti-probing countermeasures to IC designers

assessment_methods.description: Using a decapped target IC on a probe station, identify target signals, make electrical contact, and extract meaningful data from internal IC buses
Observe probe needle manipulation technique, signal identification methodology, and ESD safety compliance during a live probing session

equipment: Manual or semi-automated probe station (e.g., FormFactor/Cascade Microtech, MPI)
Tungsten and platinum probe needles (various tip radii)
Probe station microscope with high-magnification optics
